description: Organism Identification Atlas. Phase 1 entries are text-only reference descriptions at genus level; no images are reused without a license. Toxin associations describe what has been reported for some strains in the genus — never what a particular sample contains.

categories.name: Cyanobacteria
categories.summary: Photosynthetic bacteria: single cells, colonies or filaments, no chloroplasts or nucleus.

categories.name: Green algae
categories.summary: Eukaryotic algae with grass-green chloroplasts — common look-alikes for cyanobacteria in ponds and streams.

categories.name: Diatoms
categories.summary: Eukaryotic algae with glass (silica) cell walls; dominant on many stream rocks.

categories.name: Other freshwater protists
categories.summary: Euglenoids, dinoflagellates, ciliates, amoebae and flagellates.

categories.name: Zooplankton
categories.summary: Rotifers, copepods and cladocerans that graze phytoplankton.

categories.name: Aquatic macroinvertebrates
categories.summary: Insect larvae, snails, crustaceans and worms visible without a microscope; classic stream-health indicators.

diagnostic_morphology: Small spherical cells (a few micrometers across) packed irregularly in a shared mucilage colony
Cells look dark or shimmering because they contain gas vesicles
Colonies range from small clusters to large, irregular, sometimes perforated masses visible to the eye as green 'paint flecks'
records.typical_habitat: Planktonic in warm, calm, nutrient-rich lakes, reservoirs and ponds; overwinters on sediments.
records.ecological_function: Primary producer; the most widespread bloom-former in eutrophic fresh water. Large colonies resist grazing.
similar_taxa: Other colonial coccoid cyanobacteria (e.g., Aphanocapsa, Woronichinia, Snowella)
Colonial green algae (have chloroplasts and lack gas vesicles)
records.identification_limits: Species have traditionally been named from colony shape and mucilage, which change with conditions and in culture; genetic studies do not support many morphospecies. Toxic and non-toxic strains look the same.

toxin_associations.note: Many, but not all, strains carry microcystin-synthesis genes; the share of toxic genotypes in a population varies.

records.status_note: Genus-level reference description; no images yet.

records.authority: (Ralfs ex Bornet & Flahault) P. Wacklin, L. Hoffmann & J. Komárek
diagnostic_morphology: Chains (trichomes) of round to barrel-shaped cells, straight or coiled
Gas vesicles in vegetative cells
Heterocytes spaced along the filament (intercalary); larger akinetes may be present
records.typical_habitat: Planktonic in lakes, reservoirs and ponds; often in summer when dissolved nitrogen is low.
records.identification_limits: Species are distinguished by coiling, cell and akinete dimensions and akinete position, which overlap; molecular data are needed for confident species names.

toxin_associations.note: Reported from some strains; many strains also produce taste-and-odor compounds such as geosmin.

records.status_note: Genus-level reference description; no images yet.

diagnostic_morphology: Straight filaments, often aggregated side by side into flakes or bundles that look like floating grass clippings
End cells elongated and pale
Intercalary heterocytes and elongated akinetes; gas vesicles present
records.typical_habitat: Planktonic in nutrient-rich lakes and reservoirs, including cooler waters.
records.identification_limits: The traditional genus contains at least five phylogenetically distant groups; several former species now belong to other genera.

toxin_associations.note: Reported from some members of the traditional genus and related genera; varies by strain.

records.status_note: Genus-level reference description; no images yet.

former_names: Oscillatoria (planktonic species such as O. agardhii and O. rubescens)
diagnostic_morphology: Solitary, straight, unbranched filaments without heterocytes or akinetes
Cells shorter than wide, with gas vesicles
Some species are red-pigmented (phycoerythrin-rich) and live deep in stratified lakes
records.typical_habitat: Planktonic in shallow turbid lakes (P. agardhii) and deep stratified lakes (P. rubescens).
records.ecological_function: Primary producer that tolerates low light.
records.identification_limits: Separation from similar unbranched filaments needs gas-vesicle observation and cell dimensions; species identity often requires molecular data.

toxin_associations.note: Commonly reported; toxic and non-toxic strains co-occur.

records.status_note: Genus-level reference description; no images yet.

diagnostic_morphology: Unbranched filaments of short, disc-like cells (much wider than long)
No heterocytes or akinetes
Filaments glide and slowly rotate or wave — the 'oscillating' movement behind the name
records.typical_habitat: Benthic mats on sediment, rocks and wood in streams, ponds and lake margins; some in the plankton.
records.ecological_function: Primary producer; mat-former that stabilizes sediments.
records.identification_limits: 'Oscillatoria' was historically used for almost any unbranched filament of this type. Many such organisms now belong to other genera, so older reports — including toxin reports — may refer to different taxa. Treat field identifications as a morphotype ('Oscillatoria-like').

toxin_associations.note: Older reports under this name often concern organisms now placed in other genera; check the current name of any cited strain.

records.status_note: Treated as a morphotype group, not a single genus.

former_names: Cylindrospermopsis (e.g., C. raciborskii, now R. raciborskii)
diagnostic_morphology: Solitary, short to medium filaments, straight, curved or coiled, often tapering at the ends
When present, heterocytes are at the filament ends (terminal), not along the middle
Akinetes may form near the ends or along the filament
records.typical_habitat: Planktonic in warm, often turbid lakes and reservoirs; has expanded into temperate regions.
records.ecological_function: Primary producer; competitive under low light and variable nutrients.
similar_taxa: Other Nostocales filaments without visible heterocytes
records.identification_limits: Raphidiopsis and Cylindrospermopsis were separated only by the presence of heterocytes, which can be absent; genetic data supported uniting them. Filaments without heterocytes are easy to misidentify.

toxin_associations.note: Production differs among strains and regions.

records.status_note: Genus-level reference description; no images yet.

records.common_name: Star jelly; witch's butter (for some terrestrial colonies)
diagnostic_morphology: Bead-like chains of round cells tangled inside a firm, shared gelatinous matrix
Colonies form jelly balls, sheets or crusts visible to the naked eye
Intercalary heterocytes; akinetes in some species
records.typical_habitat: On soil, rocks and plants in damp places, attached in streams and ponds; also as symbionts of some plants and fungi (lichens).
records.ecological_function: Nitrogen fixer that adds nitrogen to soils and partner organisms.
records.identification_limits: Colony form is helpful but several genera have been split from Nostoc on genetic grounds.

toxin_associations.note: Reported from some strains; most Nostoc are not known bloom-formers.

records.status_note: Genus-level reference description; no images yet.

former_names: Phormidium autumnale group (now Microcoleus autumnalis and relatives)
diagnostic_morphology: Unbranched filaments without heterocytes, single or bundled within a common sheath
End cell often rounded or capped (a calyptra)
Forms dark green to brown-black leathery mats on rocks and gravel
records.typical_habitat: Benthic in streams and rivers, especially on cobbles in clear, flowing water; also soils and desert crusts.
records.ecological_function: Primary producer and mat-builder; mats can detach and float downstream.
records.identification_limits: Requires careful observation of sheaths, end cells and cell dimensions; reassignments from Phormidium are recent, so older literature uses other names.

toxin_associations.note: Benthic mats of this group have been linked to dog deaths in rivers elsewhere; toxicity varies greatly among mats.

records.status_note: Highly relevant to stream sites such as Allen Branch; no local records yet.

diagnostic_morphology: Body enclosed in a clear, two-sided carapace ending in a tail spine
Large compound eye; branched second antennae used for swimming in jerky hops
Filtering legs visible beating inside the carapace; eggs often visible in a dorsal brood chamber
records.typical_habitat: Ponds and lakes; rare in fast-flowing streams.
records.ecological_function: Key filter-feeding grazer linking phytoplankton to fish; target of biomanipulation.
records.identification_limits: Species identification needs close examination of the head, spines and postabdomen; hybrids occur.
records.status_note: Included as the model grazer discussed in Chapter 6.
